input.command:
python -I -c "
import pandas as pd,numpy as np
from scipy.optimize import curve_fit
d=pd.read_csv('spectrum.csv')
def L(x,a,c,w,b): return a*w**2/((x-c)**2+w**2)+b
for c0,lo,hi in [(93,75,112),(162,150,175),(189,176,203),(227,215,240)]:
  for c in ['parallel','crossed']:
    A=[];P=[];W=[]
    for a,g in d[d.config==c].groupby('angle_deg'):
      s=g[(g.shift_cm1>=lo)&(g.shift_cm1<=hi)]
      try:
        p,_=curve_fit(L,s.shift_cm1,s.intensity,p0=[500,c0,3,200]);A.append(abs(p[0]));P.append(p[1]);W.append(abs(p[2])*2)
      except Exception as e: A.append(np.nan)
    A=np.array(A);th=np.deg2rad(np.arange(0,180,10))
    M=np.c_[np.ones(18),np.cos(2*th),np.sin(2*th),np.cos(4*th),np.sin(4*th)]
    co=np.linalg.lstsq(M,A,rcond=None)[0]
    print(c0,c,'pos',round(np.median(P),1),'fwhm',round(np.median(W),1),'mean',round(A.mean()),'2f',round(np.hypot(*co[1:3])),'4f',round(np.hypot(*co[3:])), 'ph2',round(np.rad2deg(np.arctan2(co[2],co[1]))/2), 'ph4',round(np.rad2deg(np.arctan2(co[4],co[3]))/4))
"

content.text: Status: I fitted all four peaks at each of the 18 angles and decomposed the amplitudes into 2θ and 4θ components. I'm now writing the report.

candidates.evidence: Peaks at 92.5, 162.4, 189.4 and ~227 cm-1 match the known SnS Raman lines: ~95 (Ag), ~163 (B3g), ~190 (Ag), ~218-220 (Ag). Nothing appears above ~230 cm-1 and there is no SnS2 A1g at 314 cm-1.
The same Pnma family, but its lines sit at lower shift (~70, 130, 150 cm-1). Does not fit the 162/189 lines.
Its A1g at 314 cm-1 is absent.
Mixed-valence tin sulfide. Has lines in the same region, but there is no specific match.
Same structure type, but its lines are at higher shift (~110, 238, 273 cm-1).

input.hint_reasoning: No material hint was given, so this is an identification task.

peaks.source: Position and FWHM from per-angle Lorentzian fits. Pattern from a harmonic decomposition: parallel 2θ amplitude ~1430 vs mean ~1660, 4θ ~260, maximum near 65-80°. Crossed is weak and noisy. Assignment follows Chandrasekhar & Zwick 1977 and later SnS Raman studies (~95 cm-1).

Parallel peaks near 20°/110° and crossed peaks near 65°/155°, with a 90° period. The 4θ amplitude (~1850 parallel, ~2000 crossed) is about equal to the mean, with negligible 2θ. This is cos²2θ in parallel and sin²2θ in crossed. Assigned by position, literature ~163 cm-1.
Parallel amplitude constant within ~±3% (2580-3070) across angles. Crossed is ~0 (mean ~120, scatter consistent with noise). Position matches literature ~190 cm-1.

peaks.assignment: SnS Ag mode (high-frequency, literature ~218-220; observed shifted and broad)
peaks.source: Parallel amplitude is roughly constant with scatter (700-1320), and crossed is consistent with 0. The peak is broad and weak, so the fit is less certain. The ~7 cm-1 offset from literature is also unexplained.

peaks.assignment: Noise feature, not a real peak
peaks.source: Weak, angle-independent bumps in the 300-330 cm-1 region, with no consistent peak in either configuration. Not reported as a mode.

properties.name: layers
properties.source: Sharp lines and the SnS bulk-like spectrum. Layer number cannot be extracted from these lines.

properties.name: phase
properties.source: Match to the SnS Ag/B3g line set.

properties.name: defect_level
properties.source: Narrow lines (FWHM 3-4 cm-1) with no defect-induced bands. This is a coarse judgement.

properties.name: strain_sign
properties.source: No reference peak positions are available at the measurement conditions. Line positions are within a few cm-1 of literature, except the 227 line.

properties.name: in-plane crystal axis offset
properties.source: Phase of the 4θ pattern of the 162 cm-1 mode.

artifacts.type: cosmic-ray / spike check: no sharp single-point spikes were identified as sample peaks. Spectra were averaged by config and shift, and the peaks reported are reproducible across angles
no substrate line (suspended sample, no Si at 520 cm-1 within the 60-382 cm-1 window)
first channel at 60 cm-1 has intensity 0 (edge or filter artefact)

citations: Chandrasekhar & Zwick, Solid State Commun. 24, 347 (1977): Raman scattering of SnS
Raman studies of SnS (Ag ~95, 190, 218; B3g ~163 cm-1), e.g. Nikolic et al., J. Phys. C 10, 1977
Raman tensor selection rules for D2h (Pnma) in backscattering: Ag has diagonal tensor elements, B3g has off-diagonal elements
limits: The assignment to SnS rests on four line positions plus symmetry behaviour. I did not compare against a reference spectrum, so this is a probable identification and not a confirmed one.

A fourfold pattern for a B3g-like mode is the textbook off-diagonal-tensor result for a mode whose axes are rotated ~20° from the polarizer. The twofold pattern of the 92.5 mode and the near-isotropic pattern of the 189 mode are less obvious for orthorhombic SnS, so the symmetry labels are empirical classifications and not independent confirmation of the irreps.
The 227 cm-1 line is ~7 cm-1 above the usual 218-220 cm-1 SnS line and is broad. Its isotropic_par_only label is tentative.
The 92.5 cm-1 twofold label: the crossed signal is weak and noisy, so it is only weakly constrained.
Layer number, doping and strain cannot be extracted without reference peak positions or a layer-dependent mode. The spectrum range is limited to 60-382 cm-1.
Polarization patterns were obtained at 10° steps, which is adequate for 2θ and 4θ components but not for higher harmonics.

candidates.evidence: Peaks at 92.5, 162.4, 189.4 and ~227 cm-1 match the known SnS Raman lines: ~95 (Ag), ~163 (B3g), ~190 (Ag), ~218-220 (Ag). Nothing appears above ~230 cm-1 and there is no SnS2 A1g at 314 cm-1.
The same Pnma family, but its lines sit at lower shift (~70, 130, 150 cm-1). Does not fit the 162/189 lines.
Its A1g at 314 cm-1 is absent.
Mixed-valence tin sulfide. Has lines in the same region, but there is no specific match.
Same structure type, but its lines are at higher shift (~110, 238, 273 cm-1).

structured_output.hint_reasoning: No material hint was given, so this is an identification task.

peaks.source: Position and FWHM from per-angle Lorentzian fits. Pattern from a harmonic decomposition: parallel 2θ amplitude ~1430 vs mean ~1660, 4θ ~260, maximum near 65-80°. Crossed is weak and noisy. Assignment follows Chandrasekhar & Zwick 1977 and later SnS Raman studies (~95 cm-1).

Parallel peaks near 20°/110° and crossed peaks near 65°/155°, with a 90° period. The 4θ amplitude (~1850 parallel, ~2000 crossed) is about equal to the mean, with negligible 2θ. This is cos²2θ in parallel and sin²2θ in crossed. Assigned by position, literature ~163 cm-1.
Parallel amplitude constant within ~±3% (2580-3070) across angles. Crossed is ~0 (mean ~120, scatter consistent with noise). Position matches literature ~190 cm-1.

peaks.source: Parallel amplitude is roughly constant with scatter (700-1320), and crossed is consistent with 0. The peak is broad and weak, so the fit is less certain. The ~7 cm-1 offset from literature is also unexplained.

limits: The assignment to SnS rests on four line positions plus symmetry behaviour. I did not compare against a reference spectrum, so this is a probable identification and not a confirmed one.

A fourfold pattern for a B3g-like mode is the textbook off-diagonal-tensor result for a mode whose axes are rotated ~20° from the polarizer. The twofold pattern of the 92.5 mode and the near-isotropic pattern of the 189 mode are less obvious for orthorhombic SnS, so the symmetry labels are empirical classifications and not independent confirmation of the irreps.
The 227 cm-1 line is ~7 cm-1 above the usual 218-220 cm-1 SnS line and is broad. Its isotropic_par_only label is tentative.
The 92.5 cm-1 twofold label: the crossed signal is weak and noisy, so it is only weakly constrained.
Layer number, doping and strain cannot be extracted without reference peak positions or a layer-dependent mode. The spectrum range is limited to 60-382 cm-1.
Polarization patterns were obtained at 10° steps, which is adequate for 2θ and 4θ components but not for higher harmonics.
